lots.what_it_is: Mixed lot of five small framed decorative and amateur works: a watercolour of a three-masted barge at a wharf signed lower left in red 'C H Greaves' (signature read in photo 2); an oleograph-look picture of a young woman with a basket by a river in a gilt frame; an unsigned watercolour of a hill, pines and a gate; an unsigned loose modern watercolour of gum trees in an oak frame; an unsigned amateur oil of a ruined red church in a whitewashed frame.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The researcher reported no entries and no market for a 'C H Greaves' was found. Generic decorative group lot.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep and flip maximums are 0. Judged on the photos alone: an ordinary group of minor decorative and amateur pictures, the kind of mixed lot that usually makes tens of dollars, not hundreds. The only signed piece is by an untraced 'C H Greaves' (not Walter or Henry Greaves of Chelsea).
lots.confidence_reason: Signature read, but no market evidence of any kind for the artist or the group.
lots.dropped_entries: None to drop; researcher supplied no entries. No new searches possible (session web search budget exhausted).
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2: 'CHGreaves' in red lower left, legible, painted in the same wash as the picture. Photo 3: the woman by the river has the smooth, even surface of an oleograph or overpainted print rather than a hand-painted oil. Photo 5: gum tree watercolour is loose and amateur. Photo 6: church oil is amateur, some paint loss or abrasion to the sky.
lots.condition: From photos: frames with wear, gilt frame on the woman picture looks intact, church oil in a worn whitewashed frame. Glass and paper condition not checkable.

lots.guide_summary: 7 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. The 5 close sold results run AUD 150 to 600, with four of them between 150 and 280 (median 240); the 600 is an outlier. Two category-guide sales at 70 (small, damaged) and 120 (larger board). All prices are AUD, no conversion. The researcher filed all seven as ASKING at the estimates; the opened pages show every one sold, and sold prices mostly came in below the low estimate.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD = AUD 150 (For-Auction, Oct 2025). 150 / 1.22 = 122.95, rounded down to $120. All-in at $120 hammer = $146.40. Flip: likely resale = median of close SOLD = $240. Resold through an Australian auction house, assume 15% seller commission ($36) plus about $10 lot and photo fees, pickup so $0 outbound postage: net about $194. 194 / 2.44 = 79.5, rounded down to $75. All-in at $75 = $91.50. Caveat: the sold prices come from each Invaluable page's embedded data (isLotSold true, currentBid) because the visible sold line needs a login; I take currentBid on a sold lot to be the hammer.
lots.confidence_reason: Signature clearly read and five close sold results, which would normally give High. Held at Medium because the prices come from page data rather than a visible 'sold for' line, and the paper condition cannot be judged from the photos.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. All seven researcher entries were moved from ASKING to SOLD after the opened pages showed isLotSold true with a final price.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 2: signature 'DESMOND EBATARINJA' in purple capitals lower left, legible and consistent with his usual placement. Photo 3: typical Hermannsburg ghost gums against purple-pink ranges, competent and clean. Photo 1: cream window mount, ribbed pale frame, Armitage lot tag 62.
lots.condition: From photos: image looks bright with no obvious foxing, tears or water marks; mount has mild toning. Glass, backing and any fading under the mount are not visible.
lots.question_for_armitage: Any foxing, fading or staining to the paper, is the glass intact, and are there any gallery or provenance labels on the back?

Conditional only, if a Louis Poulsen label or stamp is confirmed: keep = lowest SOLD 416 / 1.22 = 341, so $340 (all-in $414.80), leaning on a 2019 result; using only the 2026 result, 486 / 1.22 = 398, so $395. Flip if genuine: resale about 486 through an auction, less 15% commission ($73) and $10 fees, pickup so $0 postage, net about 403; 403 / 2.44 = 165, so $165. These are not recommended until the label is seen.

lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1 and 3: blue reflector ring and violet rods present, inner cones white; no red small reflector visible, whereas a classic PH5 usually has a red one (Sworders' example also mentions only blue). Photo 2: plain white cylindrical socket housing with no visible label; the flex near the canopy looks untidy with what may be exposed wire or a loose connector beside the top shade. Proportions (about 50 x 24 cm) match a PH5.
lots.condition: From photos: shades look straight and the white paint is fairly clean, with some marks on the top shade. Wiring looks old and untidy near the canopy and would need checking or replacing. Authenticity unknown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there a Louis Poulsen label, stamp or embossing inside the top canopy, on the socket housing or on any shade? Is a small red reflector cone present? What is the state of the wiring near the top shade?
